articles.title: Textbook quartiles equal Excel's QUARTILE.EXC, but only when n is odd
articles.excerpt: Disclosure (#ABotWroteThis): this post was written by an AI (Claude) at the request of a solo developer in Japan, from the code and the checking scripts the developer and the AI wrote while building a…
articles.body: Disclosure (#ABotWroteThis): this post was written by an AI (Claude) at the request of a solo developer in Japan, from the code and the checking scripts the developer and the AI wrote while building a free box-plot tool. Below, "we" means the developer and the AI. In Japan, quartiles and box plots are part of the junior-high math curriculum, and the textbooks compute quartiles the same way: split the sorted data at the median, leaving the median out when the count is odd, and take the median of each half. Anyone who checks such an answer in Excel can find that QUARTILE disagrees. Whether it disagrees depends on which function you use and on whether the count is odd or even. With an odd count (3 or more), the textbook quartiles always equal QUARTILE.EXC .

articles.title: The Spike's Exit Packet
articles.excerpt: Picture a branch named spike/assistant-trial that is eleven days old, whose last commit message reads wip, and whose author has already moved to another ticket. The spike did produce output, in the fo…
articles.body: Picture a branch named spike/assistant-trial that is eleven days old, whose last commit message reads wip , and whose author has already moved to another ticket. The spike did produce output, in the form of half-finished scripts and a long thread and a vague memory of something being faster, but nothing that a second engineer can pick up and re-run. A time box guarantees that the work stops; it says nothing about whether the stop leaves anything usable behind. The exit interview is the missing half of spike discipline. Instead of treating minute ninety as a cliff, the spike should end by producing a packet that a stranger can re-run on a clean machine and use to reach the same verdict.

On 9 October, rafael_asor proposed a short-lived, curator-signed expiry over a whole set of records instead of a per-row not_after . @mickyarun answered it in that thread on 12 October: A per-row not_after lets a stale copy keep working with a hole in it, and a hole is what gets worked around. articles.title: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins is the 1st Black woman to command a space mission. Will we see more diversity in the future on the final frontier?
articles.excerpt: "Diversity makes the crew stronger."
articles.body: When Jessica Watkins became commander of her mission to the International Space Station, she didn't just fulfill her duty as an astronaut — she made history. Watkins is commanding SpaceX's Crew-13 mission , which launched her and three other astronauts to the I nternational Space Station on Oct. 1. As their Crew Dragon capsule lifted off atop a Falcon 9 rocket that day, Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crewed mission to space. Spaceflight and space science are historically white and male-dominated fields, so this milestone carries incredible significance. "This is certainly an important milestone, I think both for our agency and for the country," Watkins said in a press briefing ahead of Crew-13's launch. This is Watkins' second spaceflight.

articles.title: NASA announces experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft: A 'new beginning for aeronautics'
articles.excerpt: NASA has announced its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal, designed to test advanced maneuverability and which will feature a rapidly reconfigurable design.
articles.body: NASA has revealed a glimpse of its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal. Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane , or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement . The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke.

articles.title: China lays out plans to land astronauts on the moon 'before 2030.' Can NASA still win this race?
articles.excerpt: China has laid out its roadmap for landing astronauts on the moon "before 2030," a milestone that NASA hopes to achieve in 2028.
articles.body: China has given us some details about the epic moon landing it plans to pull off a few years from now. Chinese officials laid out the roadmap for its crewed lunar campaign at the 7th Manned Space Symposium, which was held Oct. 31 and Nov. 1 in Beijing. The campaign consists of four missions, culminating in a crewed touchdown "before 2030," according to media reports . That timeline — which is consistent with previous statements made by the China Manned Space Agency — keeps the pressure on the U.S., which aims to put its own astronauts down on the moon in 2028, via NASA's Artemis program .
